description.value: Meadow Creek Store is a classic general store nestled in the remote Lardeau Valley between Kootenay Lake and Duncan Lake, serving a wide network of small communities along Highway 31. Under the ownership of Mark and Kris Healy since 2003, the store stocks groceries (with fresh deliveries three times a week), local and organic products, beer and liquor, and automotive supplies alongside fuel (gas, diesel, propane). An associated on-site Bakery, Bar & Grill offers homemade meals, baked goods, and freshly made sandwiches — making this a significant resupply and rest stop for cyclists touring one of BC's more isolated corridors.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website content is fully accessible and corroborates all OSM contact fields (address, phone, website). The /store-stuff subpage explicitly lists products including groceries/produce, hot prepared food, propane, and gas/diesel/air — confirming several amenities. No mention of bike parking, washrooms, water refill, pump, ice, vending, or device charging is made anywhere on the site, so those remain null.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: A real, actively operating general store and fuel stop in a remote Kootenay corridor community, with a well-maintained website and broad product/service offering — a clear include for touring cyclists.
enrichment_extras.notes: Store also operates an associated on-site restaurant/bakery (Meadow Creek Bakery, Bar & Grill) with its own history page. The store has a post office, notary public, and copying/faxing services, making it a community hub well beyond typical convenience-store scope. Hours are limited (Mon–Sat only, closed Sundays and most holidays) — not recorded here per schema rules but relevant context for directory editors.
